faqs.q: How do I choose a good PG in Bangalore?
faqs.a: Visit the PG in person before paying anything, and check the room, bathrooms, food, security and how long your commute to office or college will be. Ask for the rent, deposit refund terms, notice period and house rules such as curfew and guest timings in writing, and talk to current residents if you can.

faqs.q: Is it cheaper to share a flat with friends than to stay in a PG?
faqs.a: It can be. Splitting the rent and deposit of a larger flat among friends can bring the cost per person close to a PG while giving you more freedom. But you will also share the bills for electricity, internet, maintenance, cleaning and food, and someone has to manage them, which a PG does for you.

faqs.q: Can I leave a PG or a rented flat at short notice?
faqs.a: Leaving a PG is usually easier, since most rent month to month and only ask for the notice period set in their rules. A flat normally comes with a lease and often a lock-in period, so moving out early can mean paying a penalty or losing part of your security deposit. Read the notice terms before you sign.

faqs.q: Are PGs in Bangalore safe for women?
faqs.a: Many PGs in Bangalore are run only for women and have security guards, CCTV cameras, controlled entry and a warden on site. Safety still varies from place to place, so visit before booking, check the lighting and surroundings at night, read recent reviews and ask current residents about their experience.
